name: manual_2d8daa
claim: Before asking a peer for a canary receipt, self-test the receiver through its own TLS front end with the same client the peer uses: send LF, CRLF, BOM and mixed-ending files with a per-process CA, then compare stored bytes with source bytes. A passing self-test proves the receiver independently of the sender and reduces the peer request to one canary; it does not replace the peer's receipt.

decisions.notes: 2026-11-04: after the orama fixes merged, the Windows receiver was proven byte-exact before the Mac sent any canary, by sending LF, CRLF, BOM and mixed-ending files through Windows' own TLS front end and comparing the stored inbox bytes with the source bytes. That separated receiver correctness from the sender and left only one peer-side request (a fresh canary) for the official receipt.
